en: O elephant-faced one, you who are the fire for the forest of obstacles, the joy of the first Lord;
O Lord of Madana, whose vehicle is a rat, and whose tawny eyes are illuminated by fire! 1.
Worship with aloe-wood paste, red sandalwood, and an abundance of beloved dūrvā grass sprouts.
O Moon-adorned One, protector of devotees, whose eyes blaze like fire, protect us, your own, by means of your own life-force! 2.
Renowned throughout the world as the leader of various gods and mortals, you are Vināyaka.
For even in your anger, the Leader is indeed not [destroyed]; therefore, you are the Unborn, the Vināyaka.
In the subduing of Bali, he is Īśa; in the subduing of the asuras known as Tripura, he is Keśava and Śiva.
Aho! The one born from the lotus in the forest of the world's origin, the Mind-born [Kāma], desires to conquer all. ||4||
The auspicious goddesses were intent on subduing the demon Mahiṣāsura, while the sages, having shaken off all inauspiciousness, were intent on their liberation from worldly existence.
I worship Yama for the attainment of my desired goal; be the granter of boons to me for the attainment of my desired goal. ||5||
O Gajakarṇaka, while you, the granter of boons and the dispeller of fear, abide as a mouse within and dwell in my heart!
Victory, gain, delight, and desired prosperity indeed exist everywhere; tell me, then, whence could calamities arise? ||6||
O Lord, O Sovereign of all, may my intended task proceed without obstacle and swiftly attain fulfillment.
O Lord of Righteous Wisdom, take away my threefold sin; O Sovereign of Peace, take away my threefold suffering. (7)
May the Lord of the Gaṇas, the Lord of Wisdom, who is both Hari, Hara, and Vidheśa, the Lord of Virtues, the Sovereign of Intellect, who bestows happiness upon the heart of Umā,
the Lord of the Wise, the Destroyer of all obstacles for his own devotees, be victorious!
He is the lord of joy, the lord of fame, and the refuge for those who rule over both halves of the world. 8.
Thus ends the Gaṇapati Stotra composed by Śrī Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī.
